title: Google Finds that Technical Debt Can Derail Coding Agents Through "Agent Distraction"
gist: Google research on hundreds of millions of agent steps shows stale TODO comments and obsolete bug references 'distract' AI coding agents into unrequested side-quests that add ~70% more steps, 77% more tokens and 105% more wait time; Google's scanner agents removed thousands of obsolete TODOs with over 95% human acceptance.

insights.claim: Google defines 'agent distraction' as AI coding agents being derailed by stale technical debt — old TODO comments, obsolete bug references and outdated specs — into unrequested side-quests that raise token use and execution time and can cause incorrect logic.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Codebase hygiene becomes a direct driver of AI agent cost and accuracy, not just a human productivity concern.
insights.locator: In a recent article, Google senior staff

insights.claim: Across distributed traces from thousands of engineers and hundreds of millions of agent steps, about 13% of Google agent sessions exposed agents to inline TODO/FIXME references, and agents acted on the referenced bug in 6% of those cases, usually without the prompt mentioning it.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Context contamination is measurable at scale; expect telemetry/observability products for agent traces.
insights.locator: Using distributed traces from thousands of engineers

insights.claim: In 41% of Google's unprompted agent detours the agent worked on tickets already closed, and in 57% on open bugs outside the developer's request scope, which investigators classified as scope creep.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Nearly all detours are wasted or off-scope work billed in tokens.
insights.locator: Furthermore, in 41% of these unprompted detours

insights.claim: A fixed-effects regression with developer-clustered standard errors found Google agent detours add 70% more steps, 77% more tokens and 105% more wait time per session.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Stale context directly inflates inference spend — cleaning codebases is a measurable token-cost lever.

insights.claim: Google built scanner agents that inspect years of git history to confirm a TODO and its intent are obsolete before submitting a PR to remove it; the cleaner removed thousands of obsolete references over six months with over 95% acceptance from human reviewers.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Agent-driven technical-debt cleanup is viable at scale — supports demand for automated code-modernization tools.
insights.quote: our todo cleaner has been able to remove thousands of actually obsolete references over the last 6 months exceeding 95% acceptance from human reviewers
insights.locator: To address this issue, Google developed scanner agents

insights.claim: Google's investigators conclude presubmit analyzers, codebase scanners and automated agents can mitigate agent distraction and improve AI coding agent effectiveness.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Pre-agent context-hygiene tooling is an emerging layer in the AI dev-tool stack.
insights.locator: The investigators conclude that tools such as presubmit analyzers

insights.claim: Commentators frame agent distraction as junior-developer behaviour at machine speed — a misleading comment that once cost a person a day now triggers detours many times an hour, each paid for in tokens — and extend the idea to outdated web pages confusing AI systems.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Stale content anywhere (code, docs, websites) becomes a cost multiplier in an agent-consumed world.
insights.quote: This is just junior dev behavior at machine speed.
insights.locator: Commenting on the finding, X user Tulasiram
